name: Threat Modeling Checklist
description: This module is a short pre-completion checklist of specific items to verify before marking any threat modeling task, implementation, or piece of work complete.
content:
This module is a short pre-completion checklist of specific items to verify before marking any threat modeling task, implementation, or piece of work complete.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Re-check edge cases relevant to threat modeling (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
2. When threat modeling decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
3. Measure before optimizing any threat modeling bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
4. Document any non-obvious threat modeling decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
5. Keep threat modeling changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
6. Prefer the simplest threat modeling approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
7. Keep threat modeling outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
8. Surface known limitations of a chosen threat modeling approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not apply generic threat modeling advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Avoid mixing unrelated threat modeling concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not skip documenting threat modeling assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Do not silently drop threat modeling edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of threat modeling correctness.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for threat modeling, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
